 Bentley Hudgins wins Georgia Assembly seat as first out trans and nonbinary state lawmaker
 The longtime organizer made history in the deep south.
 Bentley Hudgins addresses their supporters after wining election in Georgia.
 The Advocate
 Christopher Wiggins 
 Nov 03, 2026
 Christopher Wiggins Christopher Wiggins is the politics and news editor at equalpride, where he leads and shapes coverage across The Advocate , Out , and Them . Based in Washington, D.C., he oversees national reporting on the White House, Congress, the Supreme Court, federal agencies, state governments, and the political forces shaping LGBTQ+ life in the United States.
 A GLAAD Media Award-winning journalist, Wiggins has reported extensively on federal policy, civil rights, elections, the courts, and the consequences of government action for LGBTQ+ people, with a particular focus on transgender communities. His work includes cover profiles for The Advocate’s print magazine featuring U.S. Rep. Sarah McBride of Delaware, CNN anchor-turned-independent journalist Don Lemon, former senior Centers for Disease Control and Prevention official Dr. Demetri Daskalakis, and former Vice President Kamala Harris.
 In addition to directing editorial strategy, Wiggins continues to report from Washington on the institutions, officials, and movements defining the national political landscape, including the second Trump administration.
 He can be reached at christopher.wiggins@equalpride.com and followed on Instagram and Bluesky . Whistleblowers and confidential sources may contact him securely on Signal at cwdc.98.
 See Full Bio 
 Follow:
 Christopher Wiggins on X Georgia voters have elected Bentley Hudgins to the state House, making the longtime organizer the first out transgender and nonbinary person elected to the Georgia General Assembly.
 The Democrat defeated Republican Samantha Boston in House District 90, according to Decision Desk HQ, which called the race at 8:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday night.
 With 84 percent of votes counted, Hudgins led Boston 94 percent to 6 percent. 
 Hudgins, a 2026 Out100 honoree who uses they/them pronouns, will also be the legislature’s first Japanese American member, according to LGBTQ+ Victory Fund .
 Related: Nonbinary Georgia Democrat Bentley Hudgins set to make history: ‘Hope is a discipline’ 
 Their campaign emphasized the everyday conditions that shape whether residents can build stable lives: reliable water, affordable housing, transit, wages, and investment in neglected neighborhoods.
 In a May interview with The Advocate , Hudgins described experiencing housing insecurity and years of hearing loss before receiving treatment. Those experiences informed their argument that public officials should listen to people whose needs institutions had dismissed.
 “I wanted to really resonate with the shared experiences that I have with my neighbors,” they said then.
 Hudgins previously served as the Human Rights Campaign’s Georgia state director. Their organizing work also included helping residents document gun violence and press officials for neighborhood improvements.
 HRC President Kelley Robinson celebrated Hudgins’ victory.
 "The folks in Georgia’s 90th District have come to learn what we at HRC have known for years - that Bentley Hudgins is a fierce advocate, an inspiring leader, and a champion of equality," Robinson told The Advocate in a statement. "Bentley, who will become the first trans state legislator elected from the South, will join the Legislature as someone who knows how to make change in a hurry, and that’s good news for all Georgians."
 She added, "We’ll never stop rooting for our former colleague, and we are so excited to continue working with them in their new role. Congratulations, Bentley!"
